title: Disc brakes vs drum brakes

explain.say: When brakes get very hot they grip less, which is called brake fade. Discs resist fade better, so most cars use discs at the front, where most of the braking happens, and some use drums at the back.

faq.q: How does a disc brake work?
faq.a: A disc brake has a steel disc fixed to the wheel. When you brake, fluid pushes pistons in a caliper that squeeze friction pads onto both sides of the disc.

faq.q: How does a drum brake work?
faq.a: A drum brake has a hollow drum that turns with the wheel. Fluid pushes two curved shoes outward so their linings rub on the inside of the drum.

Brake fade is when brakes grip less because they are very hot, for example on a long steep downhill. The friction material works less well, and the fluid can even boil. Discs cool faster, so they fade less.
asks: Why do brakes stop working when hot?

faq.q: Why do front brakes do most of the work?
faq.a: When a car brakes, its weight shifts forward onto the front wheels, pressing them harder into the road. They can grip more, so the front brakes are bigger and do most of the stopping.

faq.q: Why do some cars still use drum brakes?
faq.a: Drum brakes are cheap, last a long time on lightly loaded rear wheels and make a simple parking brake. Some electric cars use rear drums because regenerative braking does much of the work.

facts: When a car brakes hard, weight shifts forward, so the front brakes do most of the stopping.
Disc brakes helped the Jaguar C-Type win the Le Mans 24-hour race in 1953.
Both disc and drum brakes work by friction, turning movement energy into heat.
